why: WK3: bin/kith refuses KITH_TURN_CLAIM on --launch-json (exit 10, nothing started); the NEW side runs the Rust launch directly with the variable set and prints its launch JSON, which holds no claim (the engine and a nested kith never see it)
A3-4: bash's sed fill treats & in the replacement as the matched text, so a home folder with & in it puts the placeholder `{{USER_HOME}}` into the rules; Rust writes the path literally
A3-4: bash's sed fill drops a backslash in the replacement (a\b becomes ab); Rust writes the path literally

A3-5: the text of the JSON parse error of a damaged allowed.json is serde's, not Python's (the warning and the skip are the same)
A3-5: bash prints the version twice when Claude Code is too old (`version 2.0.12.0.1`, a quoting slip in the script); Rust prints it once

A3-5: after "no agent named" bash adds a spelling suggestion ("Did you mean: ...") or "Run kith ls to see your agents."; the verb has only the first line, because the router and the host call it only for an agent that exists

A4-2: kith-sessions dies with a traceback (exit 1) on a claim file whose pid is no number, because its second pid_alive() shadows the first and does not catch TypeError; so does every other claim taken in a folder holding such a file (prune_stale visits it). Rust reads the claim as damaged: stale, replaced. Python is not changed in this PR

A4-2: kith-sessions looks a raw thread up with the glob `*/<thread>.jsonl`, so the thread `*` resolves to any transcript and claims `*.claim`; Rust accepts only a Claude session id (letters, digits, dashes) and says unknown thread

M5-2: a projects.json that is no registry makes the Python project-id die with a JSONDecodeError traceback; Rust prints one clear line (`project-id: <file> is not a registry`). Stdout and the exit code (1) are the same, so only stderr is listed. Python is not changed

R5 ports 1/4: the SessionStart hook for the session registry. The Python launch (KITH_CORE=python, the rollback) writes `<KERNEL>/bin/kith-sessions record`; the Rust launch with `threads` switched and a program that lists `threads-writer` writes `<kith> kernel threads --kernel <KERNEL> record`. Both forms are masked to one token each (<SESSIONSHOOK-PYTHON> on OLD, <SESSIONSHOOK-RUST> on NEW), and only that rewrite is excused: same_after requires OLD to hold the Python token, NEW the Rust token, and the rest of the facet to be equal

P1-15 M1: a granted shared server starts through `kith-auth exec ...` (`<KERNEL>/bin/kith-auth`) on the Python launch (KITH_CORE=python, the rollback) and through `<kith> kernel secrets exec ...` on the Rust launch, whose program lists `secrets-exec`. Only the command and the start of its arguments are rewritten to one token; the rest of the facet (the service, the agent, the server's own command and arguments, its env) must be equal

P1-12 R3a: bash unsets KITH_LAUNCH_SID_FILE for the run, but its later kith_env_sync fills it back from the HQ_ twin made at the start, so the engine (and a helper it starts) still sees the file `kith ask --bg` named and would write its own session id there; the run here drops both names and the engine sees neither

P2-3 A3: the OLD side keeps the asks as files (the live/ask folder, the ask-bg folder, the file wake queue) and the NEW side as rows of the core's database (the --daemon pass's core/ folder); what the ask verbs print and answer is compared step by step, and ask.json (the conversations -c continues, the same file on both sides) is read back by the ls steps

P2-3 A3 (design section 9, X0): OLD runs `--bg AGENT@MACHINE` in a detached sh wrapper (gone with the ledger); NEW refuses it with `use the foreground form` until the host's run door starts remote asks (S1, #1194)
